patterns.note: Status uses two shared database reads, a small row-to-dict JSON shaper, and a separate human renderer.
Focused unittest coverage fixes exact JSON keys, two-query behavior, JSON-only stdout, and byte-exact human output using a fake async connection.
The adjacent machine-readable snapshot captures one UTC now and computes request ages from it.
The existing elapsed-time helper truncates to an integer and clamps future timestamps to zero.
The requested run columns already exist; pipeline_version is non-null text and both branch columns are nullable.

risks.risk: The checkout still stamps PIPELINE_VERSION as 2 and its feature stage list begins at stage 1, so exposing the stored value alone cannot distinguish v3 runs unless another change stamps version 3.

Adding print-time age to the currently deterministic status_payload contract can make repeated direct calls differ at an integer-second boundary; future timestamps also require the specified nonnegative result.
No in-repo Slack or chat caller consumes status --json; focused status tests are the only current compatibility guard for the expanded keys.

conventions: Run python3 -m unittest test_status_json -v from tools/azure-runner (tools/azure-runner/test_status_json.py).
Use python pipeline.py status --json for machine output; plain python pipeline.py status retains the human table (tools/azure-runner/README.md).
Use stdlib unittest, asyncio.run, dict fixtures, and a fake connection rather than a live database (tools/azure-runner/test_status_json.py).
Keep console output plain ASCII for Windows consoles (tools/azure-runner/pipeline.py).
Preserve exactly two status reads and ISO-format timezone-aware timestamps (tools/azure-runner/pipeline.py).
